questions: Is a forest defined as a graph with no cycles (i.e., a collection of trees), or must it also be connected (i.e., a single tree)?
If the graph already has multiple connected components, each without cycles, is the answer 0 (since it's already a forest) or must we delete edges to merge components into a single tree?
Are we allowed to delete any edges, or must we delete edges only from cycles, preserving connectivity where possible?
Should we consider that deleting an edge might create new cycles indirectly? (No, but the algorithm to count deletions is standard: M - (N - components)).
If there are multiple edges between the same vertices (invalid per constraints), but constraints say simple graph, so not applicable.
Is the answer required to be an integer, and are there any edge cases like N=1, M=0? (Yes, but constraints cover it; output is just integer.)
Do we need to output the specific edges to delete, or just the count? (Just the count, per output specification.)
If the graph has self-loops? (No, constraints say simple and u_i < v_i, so no self-loops.)
